title: Greedy Propagation with Prefix Sums for Array Replacement Queries
approach_explanation: The problem allows replacing any $a_i$ with $b_i$, and propagating values to the left by replacing $a_i$ with $a_{i+1}$. To maximize the subarray sum from $l$ to $r$, we want each element $a_i$ to be as large as possible. First, we can independently maximize each $a_i$ by setting $a_i = 	ext{max}(a_i, b_i)$. Second, because any element can adopt the value of an element to its right through repeated operations, we can iterate from right to left ($n-2$ down to $0$) and propagate the maximum values, updating $a_i = 	ext{max}(a_i, a_{i+1})$. After these transformations, $a$ represents the optimal configuration for any prefix/suffix. We then use a prefix sum array to answer each range sum query in $O(1)$ time.

code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$, and for each test case reads array dimensions $n, q$, followed by vectors $a$ and $b$.
Iterates from $0$ to $n-1$, updating $a_i$ to $	ext{max}(a_i, b_i)$ to account for the operation where any element can be replaced by its corresponding value in $b$.

Iterates backwards from $n-2$ down to $0$, updating $a_i = 	ext{max}(a_i, a_{i+1})$ to model the operation of replacing $a_i$ with $a_{i+1}$, ensuring values can propagate arbitrarily far to the left.
Builds a prefix sum array of size $n+1$ in $O(n)$ time to allow fast range-sum queries.
Processes each of the $q$ queries in $O(1)$ time using the formula `prefix_sum[r] - prefix_sum[l-1]`, and outputs the results.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: Reading the input takes $O(n)$ time per testcase. Maximizing elements and computing prefix sums both take $O(n)$ time. Answering each of the $q$ queries takes $O(1)$ time, yielding $O(n + q)$ total time per test case. Summing over all test cases, the total time complexity is bounded by $O(\sum n + \sum q) = O(N_{	ext{total}} + Q_{	ext{total}})$, which easily runs well within the 2-second time limit for $2 \cdot 10^5$ elements.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: Vectors $a$, $b$, and `prefix_sum` of size $n$ and $n+1$ are allocated per test case, taking linear extra space.

strengths: Clean separation of logic: preprocessing via greedy updates, prefix sum construction, and query answering.
Clear loop bounds and variable names.
edge_cases_handled: Single query or multiple queries per test case.
Elements in $a$ already greater than or equal to $b$ and right neighbors.
best_practices_feedback: Use `long long` for prefix sums or range sum outputs to prevent potential integer overflow if sums exceed standard 32-bit signed integer limits (though max sum here is $10^4 \cdot 2\cdot 10^5 = 2\cdot 10^9$, fitting inside a 32-bit signed integer, `long long` is safer for general competitive programming).

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Adding `cin.tie(NULL)` avoids synchronization overhead with standard C streams, which is critical when $q$ and $n$ reach $2 \cdot 10^5$.
Prevents overflow vulnerability if constraints were slightly larger, with negligible memory trade-offs.
